title: Theorem C establishes no positive limit law (only rules out Tracy--Widom); 'crossover to Gaussian/other' unproven

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: The problem's alternative deliverable is to 'characterize the regimes in which KPZ holds versus crosses over to Gaussian or other limits' (cf. G6). The attempt's Theorem C proves, for FIXED $q\in(0,1)$, only the high-probability lower bound $L(\pi)\ge n^{3/4}/(8W)$ ($W=2q/(1-q)$), hence $L/\sqrt n\to\infty$. This destroys the $\sqrt n$ scale and rules out a $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$ limit at scale $n^{1/6}$, but establishes NO positive limit law. The genuine linear order $L\asymp n$ and any CLT (Gaussian limit, variance, scaling exponent) are merely CITED to Bhatnagar--Peled, not proved. So the synthesis claim that the model 'crosses over to a non-KPZ regime' is only half-supported: the negative half (not TW) is proved; the positive half (which law governs $L$) is not. To fulfill the problem and G6, either reproduce a Bhatnagar--Peled-style CLT at fixed $q$ (and identify $\gamma^\star$ in $q_n=1-\beta n^{-\gamma}$ separating TW from Gaussian), or explicitly relabel Theorem C as 'rules out Tracy--Widom; Gaussian crossover cited, not proved'.
